key_insight: A correct final diagnosis can mask potentially harmful intermediate decisions, and correcting an error can introduce new risks.
clinical_relevance: Clinical AI evaluation should assess the safety of tests, treatments and disposition decisions throughout a case—not just diagnostic accuracy.
method: Replayed admissions checkpoint by checkpoint, exposing AI systems only to evidence available at each stage.
Scored each decision separately for potential harm and clinical validity, using an LLM judge calibrated against physician review.
Branched trajectories at the first actionable error to compare error repair and new risks after corrective feedback.
evidence_signal: Across 300 cases from three sources, 55.2% of hospital trajectories with acceptable final diagnoses included moderate or severe potential harm; structured corrections resolved 73.6% of first errors versus 24.8% after bare rejection, but new potentially unsafe decisions followed 30.2% versus 19.7%, respectively.
watch_item: These retrospective audits measured potential harm rather than observed patient injury, and physician calibration covered a stratified sample.
paper_title: Right Diagnosis, Unsafe Route: Auditing Clinical AI Decision Trajectories and Corrective Oversight for Validity and Potential Harm
